text: On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it along with all its furnishings, and he anointed and consecrated the altar with all its utensils.
Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral houses, came forward. These were the leaders of the tribes, the men who had presided over those who were counted.
They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon from every two leaders and an ox from each one, and they presented them before the tabernacle.
The LORD said to Moses:
"Accept these from them, and let them be used for the service of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each man according to his service."
So Moses took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
Two wagons and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to their service.
Four wagons and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their service under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things was theirs; they were to carry them on their shoulders.

versions.text: But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things belonged to them; these they carried on their shoulders.
versions.explanation: The pronoun "these" has no clear antecedent in English, and the Hebrew imperfect יִשָּׂאוּ expresses an ongoing obligation ("they are to carry") rather than a completed past action. The revision clarifies both without adding content.

text: On the day the altar was anointed, the leaders brought the dedication gifts for it; they presented their offering before the altar.

versions.text: When the altar was anointed, the leaders brought their offerings for its dedication and presented them before the altar.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two parallel clauses (the dedication gift, then the offering brought before the altar) and explicitly marks "on the day it was anointed." The current rendering collapses both clauses into one and loses the temporal marker; restoring the two-part rhythm also reads better aloud.

text: And the LORD said to Moses, "Each day one leader shall present his offering for the dedication of the altar."
The one who brought his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah.

His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, brought his offering.

The offering he brought was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day it was Eliab son of Helon, the leader of the people of Zebulun.

His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

and for the fellowship offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day it was Elizur son of Shedeur, the leader of the people of Reuben.

His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

On the fifth day it was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, the leader of the people of Simeon.

His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day it was Eliasaph son of Deuel, the leader of the people of Gad.

His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
one male goat for a sin offering;
and for the fellowship offering, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.

versions.text: and for the fellowship offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.
versions.explanation: Hebrew בָּקָר here denotes cattle from the herd; 'oxen' in English suggests castrated draft animals, which is not implied. 'Two head of cattle' (or 'two bulls') is more accurate. If adopted, the same change should be applied consistently in the parallel verses (53, 59, 65, 71, 77, 83).

On the twelfth day it was Ahira son of Enan, the leader of the people of Naphtali.

His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;

This was the dedication offering for the altar from the leaders of Israel on the day it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver basins, twelve gold dishes.
Each silver plate weighed a hundred and thirty shekels and each basin seventy; all the silver of these vessels came to two thousand four hundred shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
The twelve gold dishes filled with incense weighed ten shekels each, by the sanctuary shekel; all the gold of the dishes came to a hundred and twenty shekels.
All the animals for the burnt offering were twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male lambs a year old, with their grain offerings, and twelve male goats for the sin offering.

versions.text: The total livestock for the burnt offering was twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male lambs a year old, with their grain offerings, and twelve male goats for the sin offering.
versions.explanation: 'The total livestock ... was' is slightly awkward for oral reading and mixes a collective singular with a plural list; 'All the animals ... were' flows better and renders כָּל־הַבָּקָר naturally in summary context.

text: The total livestock for the fellowship offering was twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses entered the tent of meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim; and He spoke to him.

versions.text: When Moses entered the tent of meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim; and it spoke to him.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb וַיְדַבֵּר has a masculine personal subject — the LORD speaking to Moses, not an impersonal 'voice.' Rendering it 'it spoke' depersonalizes the divine speaker and obscures the point of the verse, that God Himself addressed Moses from between the cherubim. 'He spoke to him' preserves the personal agency while keeping the same flow for oral reading.
